title: European Commission confirms October cyberattack carried out with AI tools
summary: Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said an attack first detected on 22 October was an AI-generated campaign, and internal HR applications were taken offline as a precaution; BankInfoSecurity reports most are restored. Euronews names Sysper and JSIS as affected. The Commission found no evidence of a breach affecting staff as a whole, received no ransom request, is still investigating, and has named no attacker.
plain: The EU's executive body says hackers used AI tools to attack its systems in October. Some staff systems were switched off, and it has not found evidence of a wide data leak.
exec: A public institution confirms AI-assisted intrusion tooling was used against it; HR systems with staff personal data were affected.
action: Review exposure of HR and staff systems and patch internet-facing software quickly; AI tools shorten the time from flaw discovery to attack.
date_note: Date is the publication of the confirmation; the attack was detected on 22 October 2026.

validation.note: Associated Press (via WRAL) and Euronews both report the Commission spokesperson's confirmation; Bloomberg headline matches.

review.note: Compared title, Regnier AI-tools confirmation, 22 Oct detection, most apps restored, no staff-wide breach evidence, no ransom request, no attacker, Sysper/JSIS (Euronews only, as summary states) against AP/WRAL and Euronews; BankInfoSecurity partly read
